content: The outcomes of treatment are reported separately based on prior treatment experience. The analysis of all treatment experiences combines data from patients who are treatment-naïve, treatment-experienced, or have an unclear treatment history. Evidence from clinical trials includes data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized trials, and single-arm trials. This analysis is further supplemented by an all-evidence analysis, which incorporates outcomes from observational studies. However, comparative evidence is not available, and conclusions about relative treatment effects should be avoided. Daclatasvir + Asunaprevir All Treatment Experience: In patients treated with daclatasvir and asunaprevir, evidence was available for those with genotype 1 infection and a mixed or unknown genotype population. The percentage of patients achieving sustained virologic response at 12 weeks (SVR12) ranged from 89% to 92%. GRADE assessments ranged from low to high. Treatment-Naïve Patients: Among treatment-naïve patients with genotype 1 infection (N=552), the pooled SVR12 rate was 90%, with a high GRADE assessment. Treatment-Experienced Patients: For treatment-experienced patients with genotype 1 infection (N=484), the pooled SVR12 rate was 85%, with a moderate GRADE assessment. Daclatasvir + Sofosbuvir All Treatment Experience: Evidence was available for patients across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 88% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. Treatment-Naïve Patients: For treatment-naïve patients with genotypes 1–5 and mixed or unknown genotypes, the SVR12 rates ranged from 75% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Treatment-Experienced Patients: For treatment-experienced patients with genotypes 1–4 and mixed or unknown genotypes, the SVR12 rates ranged from 75% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to moderate. Elbasvir + Grazoprevir All Treatment Experience: Evidence was available for patients with genotypes 1, 4, and 6, as well as mixed or unknown genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 62% to 97%, with GRADE assessments from moderate to high. Treatment-Naïve Patients: For treatment-naïve patients with genotypes 1, 4, and 6, as well as mixed or unknown genotypes, the SVR12 rates ranged from 62% to 96%, with GRADE assessments from moderate to high. Treatment-Experienced Patients: For treatment-experienced patients with genotype 1 and mixed or unknown genotypes, the SVR12 rate was 95%, with GRADE assessments ranging from low to high. Glecaprevir + Pibrentasvir All Treatment Experience: Evidence was available for patients across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 83% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Treatment-Naïve Patients: Evidence was only available for genotype 3 patients (N=419), with an SVR12 rate of 95% and a high GRADE assessment. Treatment-Experienced Patients: For genotype 3 patients (N=24), the SVR12 rate was 92%, with a very low GRADE assessment. Ledipasvir + Sofosbuvir All Treatment Experience: Evidence was available for patients across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 64% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Treatment-Naïve Patients: For patients with genotypes 1, 3–5, and mixed or unknown genotypes, the SVR12 rates ranged from 64% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Treatment-Experienced Patients: For patients with genotypes 1, 4–6, and mixed or unknown genotypes, the SVR12 rates ranged from 87% to 97%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Paritaprevir/Ritonavir + Ombitasvir + Dasabuvir All Treatment Experience: Evidence was available only for genotype 1 patients. The SVR12 rates ranged from 98% to 99%, with a high GRADE assessment. Treatment-Naïve Patients: Evidence was available only for genotype 1 patients, with SVR12 rates ranging from 97% to 98% and a high GRADE assessment. Treatment-Experienced Patients: Evidence was available only for genotype 1 patients, with SVR12 rates ranging from 99% to 100% and a high GRADE assessment. Sofosbuvir + Velpatasvir All Treatment Experience: Evidence was available for patients across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 89% to 99%, with GRADE assessments from low to high. Treatment-Naïve Patients: For patients with genotypes 1–3 and mixed or unknown genotypes, the SVR12 rates ranged from 84% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Treatment-Experienced Patients: For patients with genotypes 1–3, the SVR12 rates ranged from 85% to 97%, with GRADE assessments from low to high. Sofosbuvir + Velpatasvir + Voxilaprevir All Treatment Experience: Evidence was available for patients across all genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 81% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Treatment-Naïve Patients: Evidence was available only for genotype 3 patients, with an SVR12 rate of 96% and a high GRADE assessment. Treatment-Experienced Patients: For patients across all genotypes, the SVR12 rates ranged from 75% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Patients with Cirrhosis Daclatasvir + Asunaprevir: For genotype 1 patients, the SVR12 rates ranged from 89% to 91%, with GRADE assessments from moderate to high. Daclatasvir + Sofosbuvir: For genotypes 1–3, 5, and 6, the SVR12 rates ranged from 63% to 96%, with GRADE assessments from very low to low. Elbasvir + Grazoprevir: For genotype 1 patients, the SVR12 rates ranged from 95% to 98%, with GRADE assessments from low to high. Ledipasvir + Sofosbuvir: For genotypes 1, 3, 4, and 6, the SVR12 rates ranged from 58% to 97%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. Paritaprevir/Ritonavir + Ombitasvir + Dasabuvir: For genotype 1 patients, the SVR12 rate was 99%, with a high GRADE assessment. Sofosbuvir + Velpatasvir: For genotypes 1–4 and 6, the SVR12 rates ranged from 75% to 97%, with GRADE assessments from very low to high. This comprehensive analysis highlights the variability in treatment outcomes across different regimens, genotypes, and patient populations, emphasizing the importance of individualized treatment approaches.
